$comment: The EuropeDoor palette, as data rather than as prose. tools/checks.py recomputes the WCAG 2.2 contrast of every pair below and fails the build if a role claimed here is not one the colour can actually hold. A palette written only in a document is a palette that drifts: a hex nudged 'slightly warmer' in a redesign takes a contrast ratio with it, and nothing complains until somebody cannot read a link. This file has already failed its own author twice — see the notes on cobalt-lift and on cobalt.
philosophy: European Future — editorial x architectural x cinematic x intelligent
gold: None. Brass was the only gold token in the previous system and it is removed. Gold says luxury, premium, heritage, wealth; this product has to say Europe, discovery, movement, intelligence, culture, future. Cobalt against graphite reads as European digital infrastructure; gold against anything reads as a luxury travel agency.

discover.role: Light, warm, editorial, human. Where people fall in love with Europe: the homepage, destinations, places, experiences, culture, food, stories, photography-led browsing.

intelligence.role: Dark, graphite, quietly luminous. Where people meet the machine: the map, the planner, My Europe, search and filter intelligence, journey construction, personalisation, saved journeys, route intelligence, EuropeDoor Guide.

accents.$comment: Inside DISCOVER the accent says what KIND of thing is being read. In INTELLIGENCE there is one accent and it is cobalt-air, which was measured for that ground in the DISCOVER-dark block before it was needed here. It was electric lime until the accent was found to be drawing geography: every route, every dot and every lit country, which is not five per cent of anything.

structural.where: the default: homepage, countries, regions, destinations, journeys

cultural.where: stories, events, experiences — the human half of DISCOVER

heritage.where: how this project knows what it claims: /method, /sources, /fund, /sources/freshness

machine.where: INTELLIGENCE only. 7.06 on the graphite ground, 6.31 on the card and 6.04 on the deep surface, so it is a read colour on all three — which electric lime was too, and it was never the contrast that failed

cartography.$comment: THE PICTURES WERE GIVEN A CARTOGRAPHY AND THE INSTRUMENTS WERE NOT. docs/cartography.md splits every drawing on what it IS — a picture is paper, an instrument is graphite — and the picture half got a four-step ocean, a land family, an ink coast and a lit subject, every one of them measured. The instrument half kept five raw hexes invented before European Future (#0a1220, #253546, #1b2735, #4a6480, #3a6299): navy rather than graphite, in no token here, recomputed by no check. Land against water measured 7.91 on the pictures and 1.50 on /map, and a country outside the subject measured 1.24, which is not a quiet country but a country that is not drawn. These rows are the ladder, and checks.py recomputes every one from the hexes in assets/css/europedoor.css rather than from a copy kept here, so the stylesheet and the register cannot drift apart.
cartography.why_a_separation_and_not_a_claim: A claim above says a colour may carry TEXT on a ground. These say two drawn areas must be distinguishable from each other. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 puts a graphical object's boundary at 3:1, which is why the coast rows are 3.0 and the land rows are lower: a fill that reads as a mass and an edge that is unambiguous are two different jobs, and the instrument had neither.

separations.why: the land is a mass, not a hairline. Europe is what the light falls on — the hero's reading, applied to the instrument
a country outside the subject is still drawn. 1.24 is not quiet, it is absent
three tiers — water, context, subject — and each step has to be visible or there are two
SC 1.4.11: the boundary of a graphical object. The instrument had no coast token at all
the same edge read from the other side
a frontier is a line drawn ON land and is quieter than a coast, which is where land meets sea. Both were one stroke
the selected country replaces the land it sits on, so it has to clear the land. cobalt-air is the declared INTELLIGENCE accent and was already measured for this ground
the picture half, recorded so the two halves are one register and the good one cannot quietly follow the bad one down
the ink coast on paper — the relationship the instrument now has inverted

ratio.$comment: The ratio is the instruction, not the hex codes. A palette gives you a blue website with gold buttons; a ratio gives you European editorial design over futuristic infrastructure.

graphite.name: Deep Graphite
graphite.role: the intelligence foundation. Ink in the light world, ground in the dark

graphite-2.name: Graphite Surface
graphite-2.role: cards and raised surfaces in the dark world

graphite-3.name: Graphite Deep
graphite-3.role: the deepest dark surface. Chosen so cobalt-lift still clears AA on it

limestone.name: Limestone
limestone.role: the DISCOVER ground, kept from the previous system. Never pure white

limestone-2.name: Limestone Surface
limestone-2.role: cards and raised surfaces in the light world

limestone-3.name: Limestone Deep
limestone-3.role: tracks, wells and the deepest light surface

cobalt.name: European Cobalt
cobalt.role: the digital signature, for things DRAWN rather than read: the mark, score bars, map dots. 4.04:1 on limestone-3, so not text

cobalt-deep.name: Cobalt Deep
cobalt-deep.role: every cobalt that is text or an action in the light world

cobalt-lift.name: Cobalt Lift
cobalt-lift.role: links and interactive elements on dark surfaces. Chosen against the CARD, not the ground: #5070FF clears 4.56 on #101214 and falls to 4.07 on #1a1e22, where links actually sit. A dark palette has two backgrounds and the lighter one binds

cobalt-air.name: Cobalt Air
cobalt-air.role: hover and the DISCOVER accent for a dark-preference reader

atlantic.name: Atlantic Green
atlantic.role: heritage and provenance. The previous primary, retained with a narrow home rather than deleted

atlantic-lift.name: Atlantic Lift
atlantic-lift.role: the same, for a dark-preference reader: #14483c is 1.81:1 on graphite

terracotta.name: Terracotta
terracotta.role: the warm cultural accent: stories, events, experiences

terracotta-2.name: Terracotta Deep
terracotta-2.role: the same, on limestone-3, where #a4491f measures 4.48 and just misses

terracotta-lift.name: Terracotta Lift
terracotta-lift.role: the cultural accent for a dark-preference reader: #a4491f is 3.17:1 on graphite

ultramarine.name: Ultramarine
ultramarine.role: atmosphere only: gradients, map washes, immersive moments. Never type

forbidden.why: 4.04 — the signature is a drawn colour, not a read one. Use cobalt-deep.
3.52 — a UI edge at most, never a link. Use cobalt-lift.
3.13 — the dark world's link colour is a UI edge at most on light.
2.44 — the dark world's accent is a UI edge at most on paper.
4.28 — fails body text. Ultramarine is atmosphere, never type.
3.17 — the cultural accent has to lift at night. Use terracotta-lift.
1.81 — a heading nobody can see. Use atlantic-lift.

never: gold or brass as a primary, a signature, or on anything interactive
navy and gold as the primary pair
generic tourism blue as a page background
gradient as decoration rather than as atmosphere
the letters A and I in the masthead, the navigation, or any h1
electric lime, anywhere: it was the dark world's accent and it ended up drawing continents
